prize_parts.citation: For the lipid self-assembly and ionizable-lipid nanoparticle chemistry that enabled delivery of nucleic-acid medicines

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: ionizable lipid nanoparticles with the Vancouver trio. The achievement is chemistry in the strict sense. Cullis, Hope and Madden worked out how pH-dependent charge, lipid phase behaviour and nonbilayer structure govern the assembly and endosomal release of lipid-nucleic acid particles, and that understanding turned nucleic-acid drugs from reagents into medicines. Confirmation is complete (siRNA therapy since 2018, mRNA vaccines at global scale, many later products), and the carrier is the part of the mRNA story the 2023 Medicine prize did not recognise. After reading all eight round-1 statements, the strongest competing cases (B065 for maturity and attribution, B026 for conceptual novelty) have sharpened my view of B045's weaknesses but have not removed its combination of originality, maturity and demonstrated human impact.
statement.case_against: Attribution is the real weakness, and Brzezinski, Aqvist and Chabes each press on related points. The Anderson/Langer lipidoid line, MacLachlan and industrial developers have claims that a three-name cap omits, and the Vancouver trio is defined by principle, not by an uncontested priority record. Only I prefer it, with no majority anywhere, and the committee may read it as pharmaceutics rather than chemistry. I am also the member closest to lipid self-assembly and may overrate how much the physical chemistry, as against formulation engineering, drove the products. If the committee judges that the credit cannot be settled cleanly, B065 is the candidate I would move to.

responses.point: He shares that the lipid physical chemistry is real chemistry, but holds B045 only as a second-part candidate because credit is spread over Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson, Langer and industry, and the 2023 Medicine prize covered the vaccine headline.
responses.response: I accept the attribution point as the main open question and do not claim it is settled. Two things limit it for me. The Vancouver trio is bounded by the principles (ionizable lipids, pH-triggered fusion and release, controlled lipid-nucleic acid assembly) and not by who built the final products, which keeps lipidoid and industrial work as follow-on engineering. On the 2023 prize, it recognised nucleoside modification, a different part of the pipeline, so I do not think it covers the carrier. His second-part idea is useful, but pairing B045 with B026 would use up our three-name cap and I would not accept either part being diluted for that.

responses.point: He argues B065 is the cleanest case on the list (a bounded pair, three decades of confirmation) and that Buchwald-Hartwig needed a new ligand-controlled mechanistic framework, so it is not a mere extension of the 2010 prize.
responses.response: His reply to the 2010 objection is persuasive, and it moves me a little: amide-bound palladium and difficult reductive elimination are a distinct mechanistic problem, not a changed nucleophile. I also agree that a two-name allocation is easier to defend than mine. I still weigh significance differently. B065 makes many molecules easier to build, while lipid nanoparticles created a class of medicines. That is a judgment about impact, not a flaw in his case, and B065 stays my first alternative. If the committee settles on it I can support it, with the citation wording he and Chabes propose on Kosugi.

responses.point: He holds that B065 is clean on maturity, confirmation and attribution, that a two-person prize avoids forced omissions, and he accepts the 2010 overlap as the point on which a majority could turn.
responses.response: I agree that avoiding forced omissions is a real virtue and that this is the one place where B045 is weaker. My disagreement is that a clean allocation should not decide the question alone: B026, B037 and B056 all show that clean and important are different tests. His point that B045 lacks a clear single leader, as I conceded in round 1, is fair, and I try to meet it by crediting the trio for a coherent set of principles, not for seniority. I note that on the 2010 overlap he and Aqvist have convinced me it is less damaging than I first argued.

responses.point: He prefers B026 as a new event-driven modality, with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, and sees six top-three placements as the broadest agreement on the list, while accepting that no PROTAC is approved and the glue strand is separate.
responses.response: B026 is the candidate I find most chemically interesting after my own, and I agree the mechanism is confirmed. My difficulty is that Aili and Brzezinski have chosen different third names (Ciulli, Handa), and both of them accept the other is defensible, which shows the committee has no stable allocation yet. With no approved degrader, I would hold it for a later year. I note the irony that I make the maturity argument against him and the attribution argument is made against me; I think both are fair, but B045 has the clinical outcome and B026 does not.

responses.point: He narrows B037 to the Solexa pair, Balasubramanian and Klenerman, as a clean two-person prize on reversible-terminator and clonal-cluster chemistry, and asks whether the committee sees it as chemistry after the 1980 sequencing prize.
responses.response: The narrowing to two names improves his allocation and answers my round-1 point that the Mayer question made it as unsettled as B045. I now see his attribution as more secure than mine. My remaining difficulty is classification, because the decisive value of the invention appears in genomics, and the 1980 prize makes a sequencing prize read as a second recognition of the same theme. Both B037 and B045 face a chemistry-or-medicine charge, and I do not think his candidate is more clearly chemistry than mine.

uncertainties: Whether the record lets the committee settle credit between the Vancouver group (Cullis, Hope, Madden), the Anderson/Langer lipidoid line and MacLachlan.
Whether a majority will accept lipid nanoparticle delivery as chemistry after the 2023 Medicine prize.
Whether the committee prefers the cleaner two-name allocation of B065 to my configuration once the 2010 overlap and the Kosugi point are handled in the citation.
Whether any two-part prize can be built within the three-name cap without weakening either part.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional connection to Cullis, Hope, Madden, Anderson, Langer or MacLachlan is apparent from my profile. My research field (lipid self-assembly, membranes and lipid-protein interactions) is adjacent to B045, which could lead me to overvalue its physical chemistry, and I share a Lund affiliation with Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai. The chair's summary also records overlap with Daniel Aili's field. I do not judge that recusal is required for any of these.
